thread:
maya: quick sync — we need to prioritize the auth surface for H2. customers are asking for a combo of scoped tokens + org/project bindings + better API key controls. want to align on what to include in the first PRD iteration.
jordan: +1 scoped tokens first. gives least-privilege and unblock many compliance asks. can we do a minimal MVP that covers project-scoped access?
tony: scoped tokens are fine but watch runtime impact. token introspection on every request could add latency. need design for local verification + revocation path.
sophie: starting an RFC draft tonight. high-level acceptance criteria I'm thinking: 1) token validation <=2ms median on hot path, 2) revocation/denylist propagation <=30s for Dedicated, 3) audit log entries for all token operations, 4) clear migration path from existing API keys.
samir: FYI a Fortune 50 customer wants contractor-scoped API keys (long-lived) tied to projects with read-only vs invoke permissions. they prefer long-lived but can accept rotation tooling.
maya: tradeoffs: long-lived keys are customer comfort but increase risk. proposal: two-surface approach in PRD: (A) Scoped short-lived tokens (recommended) + tooling for minting/rotation, (B) Project-bound API keys (long-lived) with admin-only creation + optional rotation policy.
jordan: agree. we should also include rollout acceptance criteria: canary to 5% hostnames, monitoring for 5xx spikes, no auth failures >0.1% of auth calls during rollout.
tony: regarding runtime: plan is to do local JWT verification for tokens signed by Redwood KMS, fallback to introspection for delegated tokens. need to define token format and key rotation semantics in RFC.
sophie: drafting token schema now. rough draft in thread:
```
{
  "typ": "RI-SCOPED",
  "iss": "redwood",
  "sub": "service:ingest",
  "exp": 1710000000,
  "aud": ["project:acme-prod"],
  "scope": ["invoke:model:read","embedding:create"]
}
```
This is just a strawman. also need `kid` header for rotation.
samir: customers want human-friendly token naming + metadata in console so they can track which token is for which contractor. add `label` and `creator` metadata.
maya: good call. add admin-only `create_api_key` permission and `project.bind` permission to RBAC matrix. We need to design default roles: owner, admin, developer, read-only.
jordan: can we reuse existing org/project model from internal product? minimize schema churn. If not, list migration steps.
tony: migration notes: any existing API key will map to a long-lived project-bound API key resource. We'll add automatic mapping script for accounts with <=50 keys. bigger customers get an import plan.
sophie: edge cases to call out in RFC: 1) token reuse after rotation, 2) clock skew for `exp` checks, 3) cross-project tokens (should be disallowed unless delegated), 4) service-to-service delegation where one service mints a short-lived token for another.
maya: acceptance criteria for GA: docs + SDKs updated, console UI for key creation + listing, audit logs retained for 90d by default, regressions test suite and perf regression <5% p50.
jordan: product prioritization ask: do we split into two tickets (scoped tokens MVP + API key project-binding) or one larger epic? splitting helps delivery velocity.
sophie: prefer split. scoped tokens RFC -> 2-week sprint for core runtime and SDK support. API key console + long-lived mapping -> separate 3-week sprint.
tony: ops note: revocation mechanism — design two layers: quick denylist in-memory (fast path) + durable revocation store for historical queries. Denylist TTL must be configurable by deployment type.
ci-bot: deploy started: branch/authz-rfc-draft -> ci/build/1423 (tests: 246 passed, 3 flaky).
samir: retention note: enterprise customers asked for longer audit retention (1yr). we'll surface as enterprise add-on.
maya: timeline proposal: RFC finish by EOW, scoped tokens MVP design review next Wed, dev sprint following week, canary late next month. objections?
jordan: no objections. flagging security review required before canary.
tony: plus performance runbook and mitigation steps. add to PRD.
sophie: I'll post RFC link here when ready and add checklist: schema, signing/rotation, introspection API, denylist API, SDK examples, RBAC mapping table, console flows, acceptance criteria, rollback plan.
maya: thanks — also add metrics we need: auth latency histogram, token validation errors by cause, revoke propagation delay, number of active tokens per org.
samir: I'll collect customer-specific requirements and test accounts for early validation.
jordan: will set up PRD skeleton in product drive and invite reviewers (eng, sec, support, customers).
maya: great. leaving action items: sophie -> RFC draft; tony -> runtime perf constraints and denylist sketch; samir -> customer scenarios; jordan -> PRD skeleton and rollout criteria. check-in Fri. :thumbsup:
